prompt:
Paint ONE building for a top-down pixel-art JRPG town map, in the classic 3/4 top-down RPG view: the roof is seen from above (it fills the upper coloured block of the guide) and the front wall is seen straight on (the lower block). The attached image is an exact layout guide drawn at the final proportions: keep the outer silhouette, the roof/wall split line, the door (dark brown rectangle: it must stay exactly there, same size, at ground level, a real door you can walk through) and the windows (yellow rectangles) in exactly the same places. You may add small details (eaves, trim, drainpipe, flower boxes, crates by the wall, a chimney poking above the roof into the empty top margin).
This building: a one-storey house in a forest village built among giant trees (rustic log houses, carved wood, lanterns). roof so overgrown with thick green moss and small ferns that the shingles barely show walls clad in rough bark slabs with a mossy stone base. Windows have small panes glowing warm amber from inside (the only light). The whole image is 208 x 160 art pixels (each art pixel 7x7 image pixels).
Premium modern hi-bit 2D pixel art ("HD pixel art" JRPG look), hand-placed pixels. Every art pixel is a crisp square of the same size across the whole image (about 8x8 image pixels per art pixel). No anti-aliasing, no blur, no soft brushes, no photographic texture, no noise, no dithering checkerboards. Clusters of 3-10 pixels with clear shapes. Hue-shifted colour ramps: shadows lean toward purple/red and are more saturated, highlights lean toward warm yellow. 4-6 shades per material, rich but earthy, worn and lived-in.
Lighting: neutral, soft, even light from the upper left, like a calm overcast evening; NO cast shadows, NO night darkness, NO lamp light pools, NO vignette. (The game engine adds the night lighting on top later, so this must be the clean base colours.)
Background: fully transparent (the magenta in the guide is background). No ground, no shadow, no people, no text, no letters.
revised_prompt: Edit the supplied layout-guide image into ONE standalone forest-village house sprite. Treat the supplied image as an EXACT pixel-coordinate layout template, NOT inspiration: canvas 208 x 160 art pixels, guide shown enlarged 7x; preserve precisely its building silhouette, roof-to-front-wall horizontal division, exact window rectangles and exact dark-brown ground-level walk-through door rectangle (including any elements toward the bottom of the reference). Do not reposition or resize openings; do not confuse the central yellow rectangle with a door: it is a warm glowing window. Roof seen from above occupies upper colored block; front wall viewed straight-on occupies lower block, classic JRPG 3/4 top-down architectural sprite. Retain generous empty top margin. Replace green roof block with thick lush overgrown moss in intentional organic pixel clusters, tiny ferns and occasional barely-visible timber shingles; rustic bark-slab and carved-log front facade, warm russet/purple shadows in bark, mossy stone foundation, restrained framing of exact window positions with fine dark mullions and warm amber glass, the only luminous elements. At the door, a real operable doorway at exactly reference coordinates/same dimensions, ground-level, with wood plank detail. Subtle hand-carved timber trim/eave, optional chimney in empty margin. Premium modern hi-bit HD 2D pixel art with consistent crisp square art pixels across the ENTIRE image (7x7 display pixels per art pixel), deliberately placed 3–10-pixel clusters, 4–6 hue-shifted shades per material, highlights towards warm yellow, shadow colors towards saturated purple-red, rich earthy colors. Flat clean even neutral overcast evening illumination from upper left. Absolutely NO anti-aliasing, smooth strokes, blur, gradients, photographic texture, noise, checkerboard dithering, cast shadows, illumination pools, dark-night treatment, vignette, terrain, people, signs, text. Background MUST be fully transparent alpha in final artwork: replace all reference magenta with transparency, no magenta fringe. Match original image dimensions and composition precisely.
